question: How often can screening many blends on 808 rows produce a seemingly strong winner by chance, and do its rankings survive another internal panel?
analysis: Use the same 27 frozen supervised probability banks and four positive shares; retain the previous research reference. At a fixed .25 share compute Spearman correlation of relative accuracy across the three original panels, and count first-panel gains that improve on both subsequent panels. Simulate 4000 zero-direction panels by flipping each group's paired gain signs together for all 108 contenders. Report the median and 95th percentile of the maximum net gain, plus frequency of reaching the observed best. Repeat grouping by identical rows and by the recurring profile detected in the fitting features. This diagnoses selection variability conditional on already developed proposals. It is not an unbiased significance test or an upper limit on accuracy.
